title: Start your first lesson
description: Open Keating, connect a model, and turn one question into a conversation you can return to.

sections.heading: 1. Open your learning space

screenshots.alt: Keating's empty chat with the Sessions panel on the left, suggested starting points, and the message box below.
screenshots.caption: Earlier tutorial capture of the chat workspace. Sessions sit on the left and the message box is at the bottom. The first-visit walkthrough and header labels have since changed; follow the steps in this guide.

paragraphs: Open Keating in your browser. You can begin on a phone, tablet, or computer without installing an app. Use the browser profile where you want to keep your lessons: browser sessions and settings are saved locally.

On your first visit, Welcome to Keating walks you through model access, setup, and a starting point. Choose Next to continue. Go straight to chat skips the walkthrough; you can still connect a model from the chat header or Settings.

To understand how Keating works in practice, follow learner Elena Chen throughout these guides. Elena is a backend engineer mastering distributed consensus algorithms, focusing on Raft leader election and log replication invariants. She switches seamlessly between the Web UI for visual deep dives, the Terminal UI inside tmux while writing Go code, and the CLI shell for rapid spaced quizzes. Use the tabs below to explore each step across your preferred surface:

surfaceTabs.label: Web UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Access Keating in any modern browser. Zero installation required, with full support for visual diagrams, OpenUI quiz cards, and audio duplex.
bullets: Navigate to https://keating.help/chat on desktop, tablet, or phone.
Conversations, settings, and learning progress persist locally in your browser storage.
Interactive OpenUI cards render Socratic checks and retrieval practice directly in the chat stream.

video.title: Web classroom entry
video.caption: Elena Chen navigating the browser learning space, model capabilities, and interactive workspace.

surfaceTabs.label: Terminal UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Launch Keating's full-screen OpenTUI terminal interface directly in your shell or tmux session.
bullets: Run keating tui inside any modern terminal emulator.
Press Ctrl+B to open the action sidebar, switch models, and inspect teaching policies.
Keyboard-driven navigation lets you learn without switching away from your editor.

video.title: Terminal UI first-minute launch
video.caption: Elena Chen launching the terminal interface, configuring her learner handle and avatar portrait, and inspecting sidepanel shortcuts.

surfaceTabs.label: CLI Shell
surfaceTabs.summary: Interact with Keating's hyperteacher directly from your shell, ideal for headless scripts and quick checks.
bullets: Run keating shell with an optional initial prompt to start immediately.
Use --continue to resume your last conversation, or --session to target a specific ID.
Supports scriptable flags for model selection and separate learner profiles.
surfaceTabs.code: keating shell 'Teach me Raft consensus leader election'

video.title: CLI hyperteacher initialization
video.caption: Elena Chen running Keating CLI commands to compile structured plans and verify concept invariants.

links.label: Watch the visual guide and walkthroughs

sections.heading: 2. Connect a model
paragraphs: A model generates Keating's responses. Choose one way to connect before sending your first question. You can change the model later by selecting its name in the chat header.

surfaceTabs.label: Web UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Select your active model directly from the header dropdown, or configure cloud providers in Settings.
bullets: Click the model name in the top navigation bar to switch between available models.
Connect via Not Organic for hosted inference with zero local setup.
Bring your own API key in Settings → Models & Providers → Cloud Providers.

surfaceTabs.label: Terminal UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Switch models instantly with Ctrl+P or manage credentials with keating setup.
bullets: Press Ctrl+P anywhere in the TUI to open the fuzzy model selection palette.
Configured providers sort first, with active models highlighted at the top.
Run keating setup to configure API keys or local endpoint ports.

surfaceTabs.label: CLI Shell
surfaceTabs.summary: Pass the model directly via command flags or export standard provider environment variables.
bullets: Use keating shell --model=<provider>/<model> to select an exact model string.
Export provider keys like OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or NOTORGANIC_TOKEN.
Run keating doctor to inspect runtime detection and provider connectivity.

Use Keating selects Inkling Small. Choose Connect or create an account, then Sign up / Sign in to connect through Not Organic. Hosted responses depend on account access and available credit; completing sign-in alone does not confirm either.

Bring your own key lets you use a model provider without a Not Organic account. Choose Choose a model and provider. Add the provider's API key in Settings → Models & Providers → Cloud Providers, or use Save key when API key required appears. The provider bills this usage separately.

For a model that runs on your device, follow the offline tutor guide. Browser models need a compatible browser and a substantial initial download. Use an offline tutor appears in supported desktop builds.

sections.heading: 3. Give Keating a starting point
paragraphs: In Your starting point, describe what you want to understand and what you already know. This is optional. Start chatting puts your starting point into the message box for you to review; it does not send it automatically.
Try: I can write a Python loop, but recursion confuses me. Help me trace a small example, then ask me to predict the next step.

Edit the message if needed and send it. You can also start with a question from a lesson, a concept you keep forgetting, or an explanation you want to test. A concrete starting point gives the conversation something useful to work toward.

sections.heading: 4. Work through the question
paragraphs: Answer in your own words, including the part you are unsure about. If an explanation moves too quickly, ask for a smaller example or one question at a time. If you understand it, ask for a new problem that uses the same idea.
For example: I think the function stops when the input reaches zero. Give me an input where that stopping rule fails, and let me work out why.

If a response stops because of a key, account, or credit error, follow the action shown with the error. Check the saved message before sending another copy. The accounts guide explains Refresh balance and Retry response.

surfaceTabs.label: Web UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Answer Socratic prompts directly in the browser chat stream with typed OpenUI interaction cards.
bullets: Type your explanation or hypothesis directly into the chat input box.
When Keating asks a diagnostic question, answer in your own words rather than guessing rote phrases.
Inspect visible model reasoning tags before each pedagogical response.
surfaceTabs.code: I think two majorities cannot overlap because each node gets only one vote per term.

video.title: Web classroom walkthrough
video.caption: Elena working through a live Socratic session: asking questions, observing reasoning, and answering the next prompt.

surfaceTabs.label: Terminal UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Answer Socratic questions directly in the terminal with keyboard-driven branching and live fork trees.
bullets: Type answers in the bottom message bar and press Enter to stream the hyperteacher's response.
Press Ctrl+B to inspect active models, thinking depth, and session policy parameters.
Fork the session at any turn to test alternative counter-examples without losing your primary branch.
surfaceTabs.code: keating tui 'Teach me Raft leader election invariants'

video.title: Terminal UI session walkthrough
video.caption: Elena Chen navigating a live Socratic session in OpenTUI: message frames, model inspection, and interactive turn branching.

surfaceTabs.label: CLI Shell
surfaceTabs.summary: Run single-turn checks, prompt-driven sessions, and automated Socratic exercises from bash or zsh.
bullets: Pass questions directly on the command line: keating shell '<question>'.
Resume where you left off with keating shell --continue.
Inspect generated plans, Mermaid maps, and verification checklists under .keating/outputs/.

video.title: CLI verification and Socratic loop
video.caption: Elena verifying Raft consensus invariants and generating inspectable Markdown checklists via the CLI.

sections.heading: 5. Return to a lesson or begin another
paragraphs: Use the sessions panel to reopen a previous conversation. On a narrow screen, Open sessions panel reveals it. Choose New session when you want to start a separate topic.

Settings lets you adjust the app and your learning preferences. The Models & Providers tab controls model connections, Learning contains teaching preferences, and App contains interface and privacy controls. On small screens, some controls appear as icons.

surfaceTabs.label: Web UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Use the left-hand sessions panel to search, reopen, or fork previous lesson threads.
bullets: Click Open sessions panel on the left rail to view your conversation history.
Select any conversation (such as 'Raft Consensus') to resume where you stopped.
Click New session (+) to start a fresh topic without losing your history.
surfaceTabs.code:
Click '+' in Sessions drawer for New Session
Click 'Fork session' on any turn to branch

surfaceTabs.label: Terminal UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Search and jump between conversation threads with keyboard shortcuts.
bullets: Press Ctrl+B to open the action sidebar and navigate to SESSIONS.
Browse recent conversations or search by topic name.
Press Enter to switch threads instantly without restarting the TUI.

video.title: Terminal session tree and resume
video.caption: Browsing historical sessions, viewing fork paths, and switching between active threads in the TUI.

surfaceTabs.label: CLI Shell
surfaceTabs.summary: Resume the active session or target a specific conversation ID with shell flags.
bullets: Use keating shell --continue to immediately resume your most recent session.
Specify a session with keating shell --session=<uuid>.
Use --profile=elena to isolate learner state and history in separate profile directories.
surfaceTabs.code:
# Resume the last active session
keating shell --continue

# Resume with Elena's learner profile
keating shell --profile=elena --continue

sections.heading: 6. Keep a copy of your work
paragraphs: Your browser's saved lessons are not an account backup. Another browser or device can have a different session library even when you connect the same Not Organic account.

Open Learning usage, find Portable data, and choose Export portable JSON to download a copy. Do this before clearing site data, moving browsers, or removing an app. The privacy and data guide explains what the export includes and how to restore it.

links.label: Save and move your learning data

title: Visual guide and walkthroughs
description: Watch video walkthroughs of every layer of Keating: classroom, terminal UI, onboarding, CLI artifacts, and the full app tour.

sections.heading: 1. Full surface walkthrough
paragraphs: Keating is organized into multiple interconnected surfaces, each designed for a different aspect of independent study, pedagogical verification, and course creation. You can move seamlessly between the browser classroom, the terminal, and command-line compilation.

The surface tour demonstrates every route in the current release in order: capability-based model selection, the live multimodal duplex room, the review desk runway, course and study plan assembly, and AT Protocol release publishing.

videos.title: The whole room in 32 seconds
videos.caption: A 32-second end-to-end tour covering model routing, live media, review workspace, return runway, courses, and publishing.

bullets: Classroom (/chat): conversational inquiry, visible model reasoning, and interactive study objects.
Live room (/live): duplex audio, camera input, and live response timing metrics.
Review desk (/review): whole-turn annotations, signal flags, and rationale evaluation.
Return runway (/coming-up): spaced repetition cards with Anki import and export.
Courses (/courses): multi-session curriculum structure and artifact tray.

sections.heading: 2. Web classroom and interactive OpenUI
paragraphs: The browser classroom is Keating's primary conversational space. Unlike conventional chatbots that return monolithic walls of text or opaque answers, Keating teaches Socratically: it reasons in the open, identifies the edge of your understanding, and hands back the next question worth answering.

As conversations progress, Keating streams typed OpenUI interface documents directly into the response stream. These include conversational Question checks, multi-session StudyPlan checklists, visual ConceptMap diagrams, and persistent SharedNotes that survive across turns.

videos.title: Inquiry in the classroom
videos.caption: A live lesson exploring why cities form where they do. Keating reasons openly, asks targeted questions, and adapts to learner responses.

bullets: Visible reasoning: see how the model constructs its pedagogical next step before delivering it.
Socratic prompts: Keating asks for predictions and explanations in your own words rather than handing over rote answers.
Typed OpenUI widgets: interactive Question cards with classification, matching, multiple-choice, and open-ended responses.
Session rail: search, fork, rename, or resume previous learning branches at any time.

sections.heading: 3. Terminal UI and branching dialogue
paragraphs: For learners who prefer working directly in the terminal, Keating provides a full-featured OpenTUI client (keating tui). It connects to the same underlying Pi runtime, preserving all prompts, skills, and session state while offering a dense, keyboard-first environment.

The terminal interface includes a responsive sidepanel, mouse and keyboard selection for cloud and local models, action rows, custom ASCII portraits, and a live visual session tree showing every branch and fork of your conversation.

videos.title: Terminal workspace and branching
videos.caption: Branching dialogue in the terminal with sidepanel controls, model picker, message frames, and session fork trees.

bullets: Layered sidepanel: toggle sessions, model selection, thinking depth, and focus mode with single keystrokes.
Fork tree: branch off any previous turn to explore alternative hypotheses without losing the original conversation.
ASCII-safe rendering: full compatibility with standard terminal emulators, tmux, and SSH sessions.
Instant /shell switch: drop into the raw Pi extension shell at any time while retaining active session state.

sections.heading: 4. First minute and profile onboarding
paragraphs: Keating is designed to be immediately usable without initial credential friction. When launching the terminal client for the first time, an onboarding wizard introduces you to the system's layout and controls before you ever configure an API key.

You can configure your learner handle, select a generated pixel portrait, choose initials, or link a local avatar image. The onboarding flow then walks through panel toggling, model inspection, and focus shortcuts.

videos.title: First-minute terminal onboarding
videos.caption: Customizing learner identity, avatar portraits, and mastering terminal shortcuts without needing provider credentials.

bullets: Local-first identity: learner handles and avatars are stored in local configuration, not on remote servers.
Zero-credential preview: test layout, controls, and help menus before entering cloud provider keys.
Custom portraits: choose between procedural pixel art, monogram initials, or local image paths.

sections.heading: 5. Deterministic pedagogy and CLI artifacts
paragraphs: Beneath the conversational interface lies Keating's deterministic pedagogy layer. Rather than leaving lesson plans and concept relationships to unconstrained model hallucination, Keating compiles learning topics into structured, inspectable files.

Using the keating CLI, you can generate lesson plans, compile Mermaid concept graphs, build Hyperframes animated explanation bundles, and run Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) fact checks. All artifacts are saved under .keating/outputs/ where they can be versioned and reviewed.
sections.code:
keating plan "Special Relativity"
keating map "Special Relativity"
keating animate "Special Relativity"
keating verify "Special Relativity"

videos.title: CLI artifact generation
videos.caption: Generating a lesson plan, Mermaid meaning map, and verification checklist for Special Relativity live from the command line.

bullets: keating plan: creates a deterministic pedagogical sequence balancing intuition, formal structure, and transfer.
keating map: turns the plan into an inspectable Mermaid knowledge graph with clear prerequisite dependencies.
keating animate: selects a scene grammar and emits a self-contained Hyperframes visual explanation bundle.
keating verify: executes a Chain-of-Verification check against the core claims before teaching begins.

sections.heading: 6. Hyperteacher architecture and narrated film
paragraphs: Keating is designed as a Socratic AI scaffold for people who still want to own their understanding. The fully narrated documentary film below explores the pedagogy, philosophy, and systems architecture behind Keating: why models should gather around the learner like scaffolding rather than a throne, and how plans, maps, practice, and verification keep the learner in control.

Alongside the documentary film, the interactive tutorial walkthrough demonstrates the complete guided learning flow: from initial inquiry to progressive hint generation, concept mapping, and knowledge transfer.

videos.title: Keating: A lantern for understanding
videos.caption: The complete narrated film introducing the hyperteacher scaffold, why it exists, and how plans, practice, and verification surround the learner.

videos.title: Interactive tutorial walkthrough
videos.caption: A 60fps walkthrough of the structured tutorial, stepping through lessons, diagnostic hints, and practice cards.

bullets: Predict before reveal: test your mental model before the explanation confirms or reframes it.
Reconstruction in your own words: Keating verifies comprehension by asking you to apply principles to fresh scenarios.
Branching sessions: fork a question into a sub-investigation without polluting your primary study path.
Full documentary narration: Kore voiceover detailing pedagogy, evaluation, and the metaharness.

sections.heading: 7. The published metaharness paper and web interface
paragraphs: Keating treats teaching methodology as serious, quotable software engineering. The metaharness paper documents the empirical framework, Socratic prompt architecture, evaluation benchmarks against synthetic learners, and the limits of synthetic scores.

The companion web walkthrough illustrates how the metaharness translates into a fluid browser experience: real-time inspection panels, model selection, live session stats, and verifiable learning traces.

videos.title: Quotable methodology and paper
videos.caption: Exploring the published research paper, empirical evaluation design, and the metaharness methodology.

videos.title: Browser application and live teacher
videos.caption: A 60fps tour of the responsive web UI, live teacher controls, and visible pedagogical steps.

bullets: Published metaharness paper: citation-ready empirical methodology with verifiable study analysis.
Web classroom: conversational inquiry with live model reasoning and OpenUI cards.
Review desk annotations: mark teaching turns with Problem, Strength, Suggestion, or Rewrite annotations.
Multi-surface parity: seamless continuity across web, mobile, desktop, and terminal.

title: Choose and connect a model
description: Find a model for your task, connect your own provider, or choose a model that runs on your device.

sections.heading: Open the model picker

screenshots.alt: An earlier Select Model dialog with search and provider filters, cloud model entries, and a warning that no WebGPU adapter was found.
screenshots.caption: The earlier picker was called Select Model and used Use Selected Model. The current guide describes Find a model. This capture also shows browser models unavailable because no WebGPU adapter was found; the visible cloud entries are not downloaded local models.

paragraphs: Select the current model's name in the chat header to open Find a model. Search by name, narrow the list with Provider, or use Use it for to find models for Step-by-step reasoning or Understanding images.
Open Model details to inspect a choice. Select a model to use it in the conversation. Wait for the current response to finish before changing models.

sections.heading: Use your own provider key
paragraphs: Bring your own key means your provider account supplies model access. You do not need a Not Organic account for this route. Create an API key with your chosen provider and check that the provider account has access to the model you select.

Open Settings → Models & Providers → Cloud Providers. For a provider with an API Key field, paste the key there and click outside the field to save it. If Keating instead opens API key required when you use a model, paste the key into that dialog and choose Save key.

Keys entered in the browser are stored in that browser's local settings. Enter keys in credential fields, not in the lesson conversation. Provider usage and charges remain with your provider account. Some provider entries offer their own sign-in flow; follow the controls shown for that provider.

sections.heading: Use Keating's hosted model
paragraphs: Inkling Small is the default offered by Use Keating in onboarding. Its account access is managed by Not Organic. Connect or create an account from onboarding, or find Not Organic Hosted under Cloud Providers and choose Connect Not Organic.
A hosted model needs a connection, permission to use the service, and sufficient account credit. If sign-in succeeds but a response does not, read the account or credit message before retrying.

sections.heading: Run a model on your device
paragraphs: Models with (Browser) in their name download into browser storage and generate responses on your device. MiniCPM5 2B (Browser) is the default browser-model option, with an approximately 1.84 GB download. Browser availability depends on compatible WebGPU support and enough device resources.

Selecting a browser model starts loading it. Wait for loading to finish before chatting. Model details shows download progress and cached files; Cancel stops an active download, and Delete download removes cached model files.
MiniCPM5 2B (Offline) is a separate choice in supported native apps. It uses the native offline tutor download, rather than the browser's model cache.

links.label: Prepare a model for offline tutoring

sections.heading: Match the model to your material
paragraphs: Use a model marked Understands images when you want it to inspect an image. Keating's current browser-model chat and native MiniCPM5 offline tutor accept text; a model family's name does not make those paths image-capable.

A recording needs an audio-capable model or a successful transcript of that recording. If you are preparing to work offline, transcribe the material while the required service is available and keep the text with your notes.

sections.heading: If a model is missing or will not respond
bullets: Clear the search and reset Provider and Use it for. Check model and provider visibility in Settings → Models & Providers if a choice is still missing.
For a key error, check the selected provider and replace its saved key if needed. A key for one provider does not connect every model in the picker.
For a hosted credit error, use the account recovery controls or Choose another model to use a provider you have connected.
For a browser loading error, read Models that run on this device in the picker. If the device is incompatible or cannot fit the model, choose another available model.

title: Manage accounts and credits
description: Understand when an account is needed, check hosted credit, and resume a lesson after an account or balance error.

sections.heading: Decide whether you need an account
paragraphs: Use a Not Organic account for Keating's hosted model and account credit. You can use your own provider key or a compatible on-device model without a Not Organic account.
Your own provider bills requests made through your provider connection. Keating credits apply to hosted services through Not Organic. Connecting one route does not pay for usage on the other.

sections.heading: Connect or reconnect your account
paragraphs: In onboarding, choose Use Keating, then Connect or create an account. Choose Sign up / Sign in in the account dialog and complete the Not Organic sign-in or account-creation steps it opens.

From chat, you can also open Settings → Models & Providers → Cloud Providers and choose Connect Not Organic under Not Organic Hosted. Once connected, this area can show your account and available balance, with Refresh account and Sign out controls.
If Keating asks you to connect again, return to this flow. Sign-in can expire. A connected account does not by itself guarantee that hosted inference or purchases are available.

sections.heading: Check your balance before adding credit
paragraphs: The credit panel shows the amount available after checking your wallet. Choose Refresh balance to update it. If it says the balance has not been verified, check your connection and refresh again before treating the displayed state as a confirmed balance.
Starter credit appears only when the wallet confirms it was granted. Hosted usage varies with the model and conversation length, so a credit amount is not a fixed number of lessons.

sections.heading: Resume after a credit error
bullets: Choose Refresh balance to check whether enough credit is available.
If purchases are offered, choose Add credits, select one of the displayed one-time packs, and continue to checkout. Review the amount before completing payment.
Return to Keating after checkout and choose Refresh balance. The wallet confirms the balance; returning from a payment page is not itself confirmation.
When Retry response appears, use it to resume the saved message. Choose another model is available if you would rather use another connected provider.
paragraphs: When the credit panel says Your message is safe, Keating has kept the message for recovery. You do not need to type it again.
If the account is restricted, adding credit may not resolve the restriction. Follow the account message before trying another payment.

sections.heading: Read purchase availability in the app
paragraphs: Credit packs are one-time top-ups. A subscription is a separate offer. Check the current pricing page and the options actually enabled for your account before choosing either.
If the app says Credit purchases aren't available right now, a pricing description is not an active checkout. You can refresh your balance, use any confirmed starter credit, or choose another model.

sections.heading: Use the same account on another device
paragraphs: Your credit balance belongs to your account. Connect the same account on each device where you want to use it.

Your local lesson library and provider-key settings are separate. Signing in on a new browser does not automatically restore them. Export your learning data from the original browser and import it on the new one, then reconnect the providers you need.

title: Use Keating on your device
description: Start in the browser, find a published download for your device, or install the terminal app.

sections.heading: Start with the browser
paragraphs: Open Keating in your browser to use the learning workspace without installing an app. This is also the way to begin when a native installer is not offered for your device.
Opening the website still requires a connection. Using a browser model for local generation is a separate setup step; visiting the site does not install an offline tutor.

surfaceTabs.label: Web UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Run instantly with zero installation by visiting keating.help/chat in Chrome, Safari, Firefox, or Edge.
bullets: Visit https://keating.help/chat directly from any modern desktop or mobile browser.
Supports WebGPU for client-side local offline models.
Local storage holds session transcripts, settings, and active learning state.

surfaceTabs.label: Terminal UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Install the globally executable CLI to run the full OpenTUI terminal interface.
bullets: Install with Bun: bun add -g keating.
Run keating setup to configure local or cloud model providers.
Launch keating tui to start an interactive, full-screen terminal session.

bun add -g keating
keating setup
keating tui

video.caption: Running keating tui after installation: profile configuration, avatar monogram, and panel preview.

surfaceTabs.label: CLI Shell
surfaceTabs.summary: Use the headless hyperteacher shell directly from your terminal or shell scripts.
bullets: Install with Bun: bun add -g keating.
Run keating doctor to verify environment detection and tool availability.
Execute keating shell with prompts, session resumption, or custom learner profiles.

video.title: CLI installation check
video.caption: Verifying global installation and running keating doctor to check provider detection.

sections.heading: Choose a published download
paragraphs: Open the download page and check the selected platform. Choose the processor architecture and package format when the page asks for them. On macOS, the choices are Apple Silicon and Intel; other platforms may offer ARM64 and x64.

Read the download's type as well as its platform. A Terminal archive opens a command-line learning environment. An app installer is a different package. Follow the link displayed for your combination rather than changing an installer URL yourself.
If the page says Not published yet, use the browser app. Availability can differ by platform, architecture, and release.

sections.heading: Install a terminal archive

screenshots.alt: Keating's terminal first-run screen with its green logo, profile-setup prompt, and Message Keating input.
screenshots.caption: Terminal startup from the earlier tutorial, showing the first-run prompt and message input. The model name in this saved capture is an example from that session, not a model included with the archive.

paragraphs: The macOS and Linux terminal .tar.gz downloads contain Keating's terminal app and its runtime. Extract the archive, open a terminal inside the extracted folder, and run the installer. Then start Keating's shell.

videos.title: Terminal onboarding walkthrough
videos.caption: Setting up your learner handle and profile during initial terminal startup.

links.label: Watch the terminal and branching walkthrough

sections.heading: Install the terminal app with Bun
paragraphs: If Bun is already installed, you can install the Keating package globally. Run setup to choose your provider and model, then use doctor to check the local setup before opening the shell.
sections.code:
bun add -g keating
keating setup
keating doctor
keating shell

sections.heading: Reconnect models and bring your lessons
paragraphs: A new installation has its own local storage. Connect the provider or account you plan to use. Before changing browsers or removing an old installation, export the lessons you want to keep.

For supported native apps, the offline tutor is an additional model download. Check for Offline tutor in the installed app and follow that guide. An ordinary installer does not include the tutor's model weights. A separate full offline edition is available only if a release explicitly offers it.

links.label: Save and restore your learning data

title: Prepare an offline tutor
description: Download a local text model, manage its storage, and check what will work before you lose your connection.

sections.heading: Check which version you are using
paragraphs: Supported native builds offer MiniCPM5 2B (Offline), a text tutor that runs on your device without provider credentials. Its optional model download is about 1.55 GB and is kept across app updates.

In the desktop app, look for Offline tutor in Settings → Models & Providers. If the panel is absent or says Offline runtime unavailable in this build, check the download page for a package that supports your device. If none is offered, use the browser app and check whether a browser model is available.

sections.heading: Download and select the desktop tutor
bullets: Connect to the internet and open Settings → Models & Providers → Offline tutor. Allow room for the approximately 1.55 GB download as well as your app and learning data.
Choose Download offline tutor · 1.55 GB. Keep the app open while it downloads.
Wait for Ready offline. A completed download is checked before the model becomes available.
Open the model selector and choose MiniCPM5 2B (Offline). Send a short text question to check that it responds on your device.
paragraphs: Downloading a model does not replace a model you have explicitly selected. Check the name in the chat header before starting your offline lesson.

sections.heading: Pause, resume, or reclaim space
paragraphs: Use Pause download if you need to stop transferring the model. Resume download continues the saved download later. If a download or model check fails, read the error in the Offline tutor panel and retry when the connection and storage are ready.

Remove download deletes an optional model download. Stop any running response before removing it. You will need a connection to download the model again. A model bundled into an offline edition is part of that app instead of a removable optional download.

sections.heading: Use the controls in a native mobile build
paragraphs: If your native mobile build includes the offline runtime, open Settings → Offline tutor to download and manage the model. Downloading pauses when the app goes into the background; return to the app and resume it explicitly.
Support depends on the build and device. A mobile browser is using the browser path below. Development previews such as Expo Go do not include the native offline runtime.

sections.heading: Run a browser model locally
paragraphs: In the website's model picker, MiniCPM5 2B (Browser) uses a separate download of approximately 1.84 GB. Select it while connected and let loading finish. It requires compatible WebGPU support; the picker explains device limitations under Models that run on this device.

Browser model files are cached in that browser. Model details shows the cached size and Delete download controls. Clearing browser data can remove the download. Keep your work exported, and check that the page and model still work in the conditions you plan to use: cached weights alone do not guarantee that the website can reopen without a connection.

sections.heading: Try your lesson before going offline
paragraphs: Disconnect briefly and try a fresh text question with the local model selected. Reopen the app if that is how you will use it later. This checks your device and installed build before you rely on them away from a connection.

Local tutoring does not make online features available offline. Account sign-in, credit purchases, remote model requests, and downloading new material still need a connection. Images need a vision model, and recordings need an audio-capable model or a successful transcript.
If you switch from an online model while it has unfinished tool work, start a new lesson or return to that model. The native offline tutor cannot continue the online model's outstanding tool call.

title: Connect Ollama, llama.cpp, or LiteLLM
description: Add a model server or gateway, choose the right address, and troubleshoot model discovery.

sections.heading: Choose a connection Keating can reach
paragraphs: A custom provider connects Keating to a separate model server. Ollama and llama.cpp can run models on your computer; LiteLLM is a gateway that can route requests to local or remote models. These are separate from models labeled (Browser) or (Offline).

The hosted app routes custom-provider requests through its server, which rejects local and private network addresses. Entering localhost in the hosted website does not connect it to your computer. Use a reachable HTTPS gateway supplied by your administrator, or a locally configured Keating environment that supports local targets.

The localhost addresses below describe each runner's local setup. For a hosted connection, use the HTTPS address provided for that service. If you want local generation in the hosted website without running a separate server, choose a compatible browser model.

surfaceTabs.label: Web UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Connect local or gateway endpoints via Settings → Models & Providers → Custom Providers.
bullets: Choose Add Provider and select Ollama, llama.cpp, or AI Gateway.
If running hosted web, connect to an HTTPS reverse-proxy or gateway URL.
If running self-hosted web locally, http://localhost:11434 connects directly.
surfaceTabs.code: Settings → Models & Providers → Custom Providers → Add Provider

surfaceTabs.label: Terminal UI
surfaceTabs.summary: Connect local daemons directly through Pi configuration or interactive setup.
bullets: Run keating setup to configure local Ollama, llama.cpp, or OpenAI-compatible servers.
Local endpoints on 127.0.0.1 or localhost are reachable without proxies.
Press Ctrl+P inside the TUI to toggle between cloud and local providers instantly.

surfaceTabs.label: CLI Shell
surfaceTabs.summary: Pass local runner models directly on the command line or via environment variables.
bullets: Target Ollama directly: keating shell --model=ollama/qwen3:4b.
Run keating doctor to verify that the local AI runtime and port are responding.
Zero external internet connection required for fully local Socratic lessons.

links.label: Set up a browser or native offline model

sections.heading: Add the provider in Settings
bullets: Open Settings → Models & Providers → Custom Providers and choose Add Provider.
Choose the provider type, enter a Provider Name you will recognize, and check Base URL. For LiteLLM, choose AI Gateway as the provider type and LiteLLM as Gateway Kind.
Use API Key (Optional) if your server or gateway requires a key. For a shared gateway, use the access key its administrator gives you.
Choose Save provider. Keating attempts to discover models. Close Settings, open Find a model from the chat header, and select a model under your provider's name.
paragraphs: Saving a provider can succeed even when model discovery fails. Read the notice, check the connection, and try a short text conversation before relying on it for a lesson.

sections.heading: Ollama
paragraphs: Install Ollama for your operating system and start its app or service. If you run it manually, use ollama serve in a terminal and keep it running. In another terminal, download a model with tool support, such as qwen3:4b, then try it in Ollama before connecting Keating.

Choose Ollama in Add Provider. Its local Base URL is http://localhost:11434, without /v1. A standard local Ollama service does not require an API key. Keating's Ollama discovery only lists models that report tool support; a model working in Ollama alone does not guarantee it will appear in this list.
sections.code:
ollama pull qwen3:4b
ollama run qwen3:4b

sections.heading: llama.cpp
paragraphs: Install or build llama.cpp using its current server documentation, and download a GGUF model supported by that version. Start llama-server with the file you downloaded. Replace /path/to/model.gguf below with your actual file path; the alias gives it the model name tutor.

Choose llama.cpp in Add Provider. Its local Base URL is http://localhost:8080, without /v1. Save the provider and select the discovered tutor model. If the server uses authentication, enter its key in API Key (Optional).

sections.heading: LiteLLM
paragraphs: If someone manages a LiteLLM gateway for you, ask for its HTTPS base address, access key, and model names. Choose AI Gateway in Add Provider, set Gateway Kind to LiteLLM, and enter those connection details. A gateway's location does not tell you whether its models run locally or in the cloud.

For a local example with uv installed, install LiteLLM's proxy package and start it with an Ollama model you have already downloaded. Keep Ollama running. The local LiteLLM Base URL is http://localhost:4000.
When a gateway routes to a cloud provider, configure that provider's credentials on the gateway and give Keating the gateway access key. The upstream provider's charges and data handling still apply.

sections.heading: When discovery or a response fails

screenshots.alt: The earlier model picker reports that browser models are unavailable while still listing built-in cloud models.
screenshots.caption: Earlier tutorial capture: the WebGPU warning applies to models running inside the browser. It does not diagnose an Ollama, llama.cpp, or LiteLLM connection. No custom-server model is selected here; check your server and provider setup using the steps above.

bullets: Check that the model server is running and can answer a prompt through its own interface. A saved address does not start the server or download a model.

Check the address from the environment making the connection. A hosted server cannot reach a service that exists only on your laptop's localhost. HTTP or private-target errors need a supported connection, not repeated retries.
Use the service's base address rather than its chat page or a full chat/completions URL. Keep /v1 off the Ollama and llama.cpp Base URL fields; Keating adds the paths it needs.

If discovery returns no models, check that a model is loaded and allowed for your access key. For Ollama, check tool support. Where automatic discovery is unavailable, My Models → Add Model lets you add the exact model ID and assign it to your custom provider.
Keep an authenticated HTTPS gateway's credentials in API Key (Optional). The current app handles its browser proxy automatically; there is no separate CORS proxy URL setting.

title: Keep control of your learning data
description: Understand local storage, choose what leaves your device, and export or restore your lessons.

sections.heading: Know where your work is saved
paragraphs: Keating keeps browser conversations, learning artifacts, and settings in browser storage. Provider keys you enter in the website are stored locally too. Another browser profile or device has separate storage.

A Not Organic account manages hosted access and account credit; signing in is not an automatic backup of your browser's lesson library. Native mobile learning storage is also local to the device. Desktop peer-to-peer sync is a separate device-connection feature, not a promise of account-based cloud backup.
Clearing site data or losing a device can remove local work. Export a copy before changing browsers, deleting app data, or uninstalling.

sections.heading: Understand what leaves the device
paragraphs: When you use a remote model, the prompt and relevant conversation material are sent through the configured connection to the service providing the response. Attachments and speech may also be sent to the services used for those features. Review your chosen provider's data practices before submitting private material.

A browser or native offline model generates locally. Other features you choose, such as sharing, online speech, or optional evaluation sharing, can still send data out. Local generation does not turn those features off.
Keep API keys in credential fields. A key pasted into a conversation becomes conversation content and can be included in a model request, share, or export.

sections.heading: Choose analytics and evaluation settings

screenshots.alt: Settings, App, Privacy shows anonymous product analytics on, session replay off and unavailable, and Arize evaluation off and unavailable.
screenshots.caption: In this earlier tutorial capture, analytics is on while replay and Arize evaluation are unavailable and off. These are the captured browser's settings, not a statement of your preferences or the options enabled in your build.

paragraphs: Open Settings → App → Privacy. These preferences apply to the browser where you change them. Controls that are unavailable in the current build explain that in their description.
bullets: Anonymous product analytics controls future product events, such as feature use and response timing. Keating excludes prompts, replies, file contents, provider keys, and full share links from these PostHog events.

Privacy-masked session replay controls interaction recordings where the deployment offers them. Text, inputs, and other sensitive page details are masked. Replay also depends on product analytics being enabled.

Share future turns for Arize evaluation is separate and off by default. Where enabled, it may send the current visible prompt and final visible reply for future turns. Read its description: some deployments permit metadata only. Turn it off to stop future submissions.

sections.heading: Export a copy of your lessons

screenshots.alt: The Portable data panel has Export portable JSON and Import portable JSON controls above a separate Training data export panel.
screenshots.caption: Earlier tutorial capture: use Export portable JSON in the upper Portable data panel to move your lessons. The lower panel prepares a separate training dataset; its older Export training ZIP label is not the backup action.

paragraphs: Open Learning usage and find Portable data. Choose whether to keep Include sandbox code history selected, then choose Export portable JSON. Save the downloaded keating-portable-data.json somewhere you can find from your next device.

The portable export includes saved sessions, learner state, learning artifacts, goals, quizzes, flashcards, and review records. Sandbox code history is optional. It does not transfer provider sign-ins, API-key settings, or downloaded model files.
Wait for the export confirmation and check that the file downloaded before clearing any data. The JSON contains your learning content as readable text; store it as carefully as the original notes.

links.label: Open Portable data on Learning usage

sections.heading: Restore in another browser
paragraphs: Open Keating in the destination browser, visit Learning usage → Portable data, and choose Import portable JSON. Select your saved export and wait for the import summary. Open a session to check its contents before discarding the original copy.
Export any existing work in the destination browser first. An import writes sessions and records with their saved identifiers, so importing an older copy can replace a matching saved record.
Reconnect model providers on the destination device and download any local models again. A successful data import does not sign you in to those services or restore model downloads.

sections.heading: Share and remove data deliberately
paragraphs: A Share session link makes the shared conversation, supported artifacts, and finalized review feedback readable by anyone with that link. Review the content before confirming a share. A share link is useful for showing someone a lesson; use a portable export to move your learning data.

Use browser site-data controls to remove the website's local data after exporting anything you want to keep. Removing a local copy does not remove shared copies or information already sent to a model provider. Sign out of connected accounts and remove saved credentials when retiring a device.
